title: Support Ticket State Diagram
purpose: Document the support ticket lifecycle states and transitions: Open, Pending, Resolved — including implicit transitions in service methods
audience: Backend developers, support team, QA engineers, product managers
description: The support ticket system has three states: Open (initial state when user creates ticket or when user replies to a Pending ticket), Pending (when admin views or replies to an Open ticket — awaiting user response), and Resolved (terminal state when admin marks ticket as resolved — no re-open supported). Transitions are implicit in service methods: user creates ticket → Open; admin views/replies → Pending; user replies to Pending ticket → Open; admin resolves → Resolved (from either Open or Pending). State transitions are NOT enforced at the database level — there is no CHECK constraint on the status column. Gaps: no Closed state (only Resolved exists), no re-open from Resolved (terminal), and no DB-level constraint enforcement.

actors.label: User (Fan/Creator)
actors.description: Platform user who creates and interacts with support tickets

actors.label: Admin
actors.description: Platform administrator who views, replies to, and resolves support tickets

systems.label: Supabase PostgreSQL
systems.description: Database storing support_tickets table with status column (constrained only at application level)

modules.label: support.service.ts
modules.description: Support ticket business logic handling status transitions via replyToTicket, appendUserMessageToActiveTicket, resolveTicket

modules.label: support.controller.ts
modules.description: Request handling for create, reply, view, resolve operations

modules.label: supportTicket.model.ts
modules.description: Database access layer for support_tickets table CRUD operations

services.label: SupportService
services.description: Manages ticket status transitions: create → Open, reply → Pending/Open, view → Pending, resolve → Resolved

dataStores.label: support_tickets table
dataStores.description: Stores ticket records with user_id, subject, status (Open|Pending|Resolved), conversation JSONB array, created_at, updated_at

entryPoints.label: POST /api/v1/support/tickets
entryPoints.description: User creates a new support ticket with subject and description

entryPoints.label: GET /api/v1/support/tickets/:id
entryPoints.description: Admin views ticket details — triggers Open→Pending transition

entryPoints.label: PUT /api/v1/support/tickets/:id/reply
entryPoints.description: Admin replies to ticket — triggers Open→Pending or stays Pending

entryPoints.label: User sends DM to admin
entryPoints.description: User replies via DM to admin — detected by message service, triggers Pending→Open (via appendUserMessageToActiveTicket)

entryPoints.label: PUT /api/v1/support/tickets/:id/resolve
entryPoints.description: Admin resolves ticket — triggers Open/→Resolved or Pending→Resolved

exitPoints.label: Ticket resolved
exitPoints.description: Terminal state — no further transitions possible

preconditions: User is authenticated and has active profile
Admin has admin role and valid JWT
Support ticket exists for operations on existing tickets
postconditions: Ticket transitions through states based on user and admin actions
Resolved is terminal — no re-open mechanism exists
No Closed state — only Resolved exists as terminal state
State transitions are implicit in service methods, not enforced at DB level

nodes.label: [*] → Open
nodes.description: Initial state. User creates ticket via POST /api/v1/support/tickets with subject and description. Conversation JSONB initialized with first message.

nodes.label: Open
nodes.description: Ticket is active, awaiting admin response. User can send additional messages (stay in Open). Admin can view (→Pending) or reply (→Pending) or resolve (→Resolved).

nodes.label: Open → Pending
nodes.description: Transition triggered when admin views or replies to an Open ticket. Status changes from Open to Pending, indicating admin has engaged and is awaiting user response.

nodes.label: Pending
nodes.description: Admin has viewed/replied; awaiting user response. User can reply (→Open) via DM to admin. Admin can resolve (→Resolved).

nodes.label: Pending → Open
nodes.description: Transition triggered when user replies to a Pending ticket. User's DM to admin is detected by message service, which calls supportService.appendUserMessageToActiveTicket(). Status changes from Pending to Open.

nodes.label: Open → Resolved
nodes.description: Admin resolves an Open ticket via PUT /api/v1/support/tickets/:id/resolve. Terminal transition.

nodes.label: Pending → Resolved
nodes.description: Admin resolves a Pending ticket via PUT /api/v1/support/tickets/:id/resolve. Terminal transition.

nodes.label: Resolved [Terminal]
nodes.description: Terminal state. No re-open supported. Ticket is closed permanently. No further transitions possible.

loops.condition: Ticket can cycle Open→Pending→Open multiple times as admin and user exchange replies

errorPaths.destination: Once resolved, no user or admin action can re-open the ticket
errorPaths.recovery: User must create a new support ticket; no escalation path exists

errorPaths.destination: Only Resolved exists as terminal state — no distinction between resolved and closed
errorPaths.recovery: Not a failure but a simplification — could be extended with additional states

errorPaths.trigger: State transitions not enforced at DB level
errorPaths.destination: No CHECK constraint on status column — application code could write invalid state values
errorPaths.recovery: Application-level validation in service methods is the only safeguard

validationRules: User must be authenticated to create a ticket (protect middleware)
Admin role required for view, reply, and resolve operations (protectAndAdmin middleware)
Status must be one of: Open, Pending, Resolved (application-level enum)
Only Open and Pending tickets can receive replies
Resolved is terminal — no modifications allowed
businessRules: Open → Pending transition occurs when admin views ticket (even without replying)
Pending → Open transition occurs when user replies (via DM to admin)
No Closed state — only Resolved exists as terminal state
No re-open from Resolved — once resolved the ticket is permanently closed
State transitions are implicit in service methods and not enforced at DB level (no CHECK constraint)
No SLA tracking, escalation, reassignment, or priority fields exist
securityConsiderations: Admin role required for view, reply, and resolve — hides ticket details from non-admin users
Users can only create tickets (cannot view others' tickets)
No user-facing ticket history endpoint — users cannot view their own ticket history via API
Status transitions are application-enforced only — no DB-level constraint
performanceConsiderations: Only 3 states with simple transitions — minimal state management overhead
No complex state machines or workflows — lightweight lifecycle
JSONB conversation array may affect performance for tickets with many messages

annotations.label: ⚠️ No Closed State
annotations.description: Only Resolved exists as terminal state. No distinction between resolved-and-closed vs just resolved.

annotations.label: ⚠️ No Re-Open from Resolved
annotations.description: Once resolved, ticket is terminal. No mechanism to re-open if issue persists.

annotations.label: ⚠️ No DB-Level CHECK Constraint
annotations.description: State transitions are implicit in service methods and not enforced at the database level.

annotations.label: Auto-status on view
annotations.description: Open → Pending occurs just by admin viewing the ticket — not just on reply.
